Paragraph 1 of a document that stands in for text extracted from a PDF. Extraction tools emit a stream of prose separated by blank lines and nothing else: no Markdown headings, no lists, no fences. Structure that was visual in the original is simply gone by the time the characters reach this splitter.

That absence is the point of this fixture. There is no heading to cut at, so the section-split branch of the algorithm is never entered, and yet the document is far larger than the hard cap on a single passage. The only thing standing between it and one enormous unretrievable blob is paragraph packing.

Packing walks the paragraphs in order, accumulating them into a buffer and emitting the buffer whenever the next paragraph would push it past the soft target. No piece of text is ever emitted twice; there is no overlap window, because overlap duplicated characters and made the reproduction invariant impossible to state.

Each resulting passage therefore carries a heading path of None, because the unit it came from had none, and the concatenation of every passage in ordinal order reproduces the body exactly once, whitespace at the joins aside. This paragraph exists mainly to add length in the same shape as the others.
